decision.question: How does one card stay selected on a persistent page, in the URL, across reloads and arrivals?
options: The page keeps a selected_id and calls history.pushState itself, plus its own popstate listener (what ai/v/3 does today)
Each card is a REAL routed page: rows are anchors, route() claims the id, and the framework's own Router does the navigating
decision.chose: Each card is a real routed page
decision.why: The rows become plain <a href> elements, so the Router navigates them, Router.mark_links() marks the selected one, Back and Forward work, and a pasted url is a cold load that just works. The page.$pages seam (core/Page's own word for where my children mount) makes the right-hand column the mount point, so the list never has to know what a card page looks like. v/3's hand-rolled version is ~120 lines of pushState, popstate and guard code; this is about 30.

decision.topic: what a new card does while you are reading
decision.question: A card arrives while a card is selected — where does it go?
options: Always insert at the top, sorted
Insert only when the list is scrolled to the top AND the pointer is not over it; otherwise hold it back behind a floating N-new pill
decision.chose: Insert only when the list is quiet
decision.why: The owner's own complaint. The DOM order is frozen while the list is not quiet, so no existing row can move under the pointer, and the sort is applied only at the moment cards are let in. Measured with a card selected and the list scrolled 600px: three cards posted two seconds apart left the selected page's top edge, both scroll positions, the first row's top and the row count all identical, and put up a 3 new cards pill.

decision.question: Unread first, or newest first?
options: Unread first then newest inside it, as the first build had it
decision.why: The brief says newest first, and unread-first is itself a jump generator: every card you open drops out of the top of the list the instant you read it, and every card anyone else marks read reshuffles the rows around whatever you are pointing at. A clock order cannot do that, because when a thing happened never changes. Unread is still carried by the dot, the left edge and the count.

log.msg: THE LINK BUG, and its cause. framework.css styles links as `:where(p, li, td, th, dd, blockquote, .md) a` — scoped to prose on purpose, so that every anchor that is really navigation (a sidebar row, a tab, a crumb, a preview card) can opt out by wearing a class. A card's links are built in a bare div, so no rule reached them at all and they fell back to the UA default: measured rgb(0, 0, 238) on all twelve links on the page. The site's own class for a link outside prose is `.page-link` (core/Page/Page.css: font-weight 600, color inherit). The fix is one word in the markup; no ai2- rule restates the theme. After: 295 anchors, two distinct colours, rgb(63,63,63) ink and rgb(184,74,36) for the active/in-path mark, no UA blue anywhere.

NOTHING SCROLLED, AND NOTHING SAID SO. The shell is a two-column grid at height 100%, and the grid's implicit ROW is `auto` — so it grew with its content however tall the grid was told to be. Measured: .ai2 was a correct 900px while the rail inside it stood 23,429px, ran off the bottom clipped by the page's own overflow: hidden, with no scrollbar anywhere and nothing in the console. `grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr)` pins the one row to the box and the rail's overflow-y: auto then has a height to work against. One scroller on the page now, .ai2-rows, which is the one that was meant to.

Two more found by looking at the screenshots rather than the numbers. (1) The N-new pill sat in the flow above the rows, so its own arrival pushed every row down 36px — the control whose whole job is to stop a jump was causing one; it floats over the list now. (2) Every card opened became a row in the site's left-hand nav tree, because route() memoises each card page into `children` and the sidebar walks that map; `leaf: true` on the AI 2 page is the framework's own word for I present myself, not my children.

assign.outcome:
**AI 2 is a list on the left and one page on the right, and nothing jumps.**

The rail previews every card, newest first, with the box you talk to pinned at its top. Click one and it opens on the right at its own address — a reload, the Back button and a pasted link all land on the same card — and it stays open while the list keeps filling behind it.

Three separate things make it hold still. The page on the right is a *different page* from the list, so a repaint of the rail cannot reach it. The rail and the page each *scroll inside themselves*, so the window never grows. And a new row only *enters the list when the list is quiet* — at the top, pointer elsewhere; any other time it waits behind a floating "3 new cards ↑" pill and no row moves until you press it.

The blue links are fixed at the cause: the theme scopes link colour to prose on purpose so that navigation can opt out, and a card's links sit in a bare box where no rule reached them. They wear the site's own `page-link` now — no rule here restates the theme.

**Measured, headless, at 1280 and 400, on the main tree's own server.** With a card open and the list scrolled 600px down, three cards posted two seconds apart: the open card's top edge, its scroll position, the list's scroll position and the first row's top all identical before and after. The pill held all three back and added exactly three rows when pressed. Reload and a cold pasted url both re-select the same card. 303 links, two colours, no browser blue. Dragging the splitter 180px moved the rail exactly 180px (331 → 504), remembered across a reload, reset by a double-click. Zero console errors at 400, 1280, 1920 and 3440; one scrolling box on the page, which is the list.

**Left deliberately.** The module is 1,109 lines against the 903 the brief hoped for — it is a second page, a routing seam, a hold-back mechanism, a pill and a splitter more than the build it replaces, and one trim pass already moved every long explanation into `doc/decisions.md`; cutting further would delete trap notes that cost real time to find. At 3440 the card's page is 2,756px wide holding 720px of prose: widening the measure trades dead space for an unreadable line length, so the gutter is accepted and the splitter is the knob. `css-scopes.txt` still needs one line reserving the `ai2-` prefix — that file was outside the fence, so the literal line is written under Open in `doc/decisions.md`.

FOUND BEFORE WRITING ANY CODE: ux/Dictate posts every finished utterance to Servex ITSELF (log_prompt() -> post_prompt()), with no `re`. So a composer that also posted from its on_text callback would log every dictated sentence twice. The seam is log_prompt(), one method — subclassing Dictate to override it is how a sentence carries `re: <card id>`, and ux/Dictate is not edited.

THREE BUGS THE PROOF RUN FOUND, all of which a reader of the code would have called correct. (1) The composer's popover was hidden with `display: none`, and @layer util beats @layer theme at any specificity — so `.flex` on ux/Dictate's own markup won, the popover stayed laid out and invisible, and it covered `+ New card` and `notes`: both reported checkVisibility() true while elementFromPoint at their own centres returned SPAN.ux-dictate-engine. `visibility` + `pointer-events` is the escape, because the markup belongs to another module and cannot have its utility class dropped. (2) The card page's three regions fell into the grid template in source order, and `.ai2-back` is display:none above 40em — so the other two shifted up a row and the FOOTER took the 1fr: 749px tall, a third of the way down the column. Every measurement still read `unchanged`, because it genuinely never moved; only the screenshot showed it. Each region names its own `grid-row` now. (3) A card page's view is cached, so a deactivated card kept its own composer and its own mic — one left listening would have gone on posting into a card the owner had navigated away from. It stops on `deactivated()` now. Found because the proof resolved two `.ai2-foot` composers on one page and picked the wrong one.

MEASURED at 1280 and 400 on the main tree's 8123, zero console errors at both. The composer block: 277px before (the owner's own count) -> 78.7px at 1280 and 73.3px at 400, the composer itself exactly one control tall, the mic inside the field, no textarea anywhere; opening the popover changes neither the block height nor the first row's top, and neither does listening or five streamed sentences. Author: 299/299 rows carry one word, 54 marked as the owner's own; `notes` narrows 299 to 8, all of them notes, and restores. No mark-read: 299 unread before a click and 299 after, nothing written. New card: mints topic-..., lands in the rail, opens with a footer; a sentence from its composer posts re: topic-..., the same sentence from the rail's composer posts none, and replaying it down the stream adds no row. Footer: the ideas' top, the footer's top and the footer's height all identical across five sentences. Live microphone with a fake device: `listening...` in under a second, the grey guess filling the footer, a settled line landing, the footer's top fixed at 151px throughout, and the post carrying re.

assign.outcome:
**Round 2: the composer is one line, every row says who, and you can talk into a card.**

**The composer.** One line — a single-line box with the microphone inside its right end and Send beside it; the engine words, the "stop after a pause" box and the assistant's note fold behind a small `⋯` that opens over the page rather than pushing it. The block the owner measured at 277px is **78.7px at 1280 and 73.3px at 400**, and it cannot grow: opening the fold, listening, and five sentences streaming in all leave it and the first rail row at exactly the same pixel.

**Every row says who** — `you`, `assistant`, `mastermind`, or the minion's own name — with `you` in the accent, because whether you said it is the question that line is really being asked. The mastermind's `Note:` cards read as notes in the rail, and a `notes` word beside the count narrows 299 rows to the 8 that are notes.

**A card you talk into.** `+ New card` puts a real card on the board, opens it, and starts listening. While a card is open every sentence — typed or spoken — carries `re: <that card's id>` and lands in that card's transcript instead of becoming a card of its own. With nothing open, a sentence starts a new card as before. Proven with a live microphone: `listening…` in under a second, the grey guess filling in, a settled line landing, and the posted sentence carrying its `re`.

**The transcript footer** is pinned to the bottom of the card's page — the words arrive there, the newest always visible, scrolling inside a fixed height, and they never disappear or move. The ideas sit above it and neither region moves the other: the ideas' top, the footer's top and the footer's height were identical across five streamed sentences at both widths. **And nothing is marked read by a click any more** — 299 unread before, 299 after, nothing written.

Zero console errors at 1280 and 400. Three real bugs the numbers alone called correct are in the log, including a popover that was invisible but still swallowing every click on two buttons.
